title: The Most Sacred Heart of Jesus
short_summary: The Sacred Heart is devotion to Jesus Christ himself under the sign of his Heart, the sign of the love with which the incarnate Son loves the Father and every person.
key_facts: The U.S. calendar lists this solemnity on June 12 in 2026.
The devotion is directed to the Person of Christ, not to a body part apart from him.
The devotion connects Christ's Incarnation, Passion, Eucharist, mercy, and reparation.

Private revelations associated with Saint Margaret Mary Alacoque are important in the history and spread of the devotion, but they are not the foundation of the Church’s faith in Christ or of the worship owed to him.

sections.heading: Devotion to Christ himself
sections.body: The Sacred Heart is not worship of a body part separated from Jesus. It is devotion to the Person of the incarnate Son under the sign of his Heart, which expresses his human and divine love.

sections.heading: The love of the incarnate Son
sections.body: Because the Son of God became truly man, his human Heart belongs to the mystery of the Incarnation. The Church contemplates the love shown in his life, his Passion, his pierced side, and his gift of himself in the Eucharist.

sections.heading: Mercy and reparation
sections.body: Devotion to the Sacred Heart is closely connected with mercy and reparation. Reparation is not an attempt to add to Christ's saving work; it is the Church's loving response to the Redeemer whose love is often rejected.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Christ at the center
catholic_connection_sections.body: This solemnity begins with Jesus Christ: true God and true man, loving the Father and all people without exception.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Eucharistic love
catholic_connection_sections.body: The Sacred Heart draws Catholics toward the Eucharist, where Christ gives himself sacramentally to his Church.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: A devotion within doctrine
catholic_connection_sections.body: The devotion is a Catholic form of worship and love directed to Christ. Private revelation may deepen devotion, but it does not create the faith of the Church.
